name: stri_split_lines
title: Split a String Into Text Lines

origin.description: Split each string on Unicode newline sequences.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: omit_empty
arguments.text: TRUE drops empty pieces. FALSE keeps them. NA is treated as TRUE.

origin.details: Vectorized over str and omit_empty. Newlines are CR, LF, CRLF, NEL, VT, FF, U+2028, and U+2029. A final newline keeps a trailing empty piece unless omit_empty drops it. A missing string is a one-element NA vector. An empty string is one empty piece when empty pieces are kept.
origin.example:
parts <- stri_split_lines("a\nb")
cat(paste0('stri_split_lines("a\\nb") returns ', paste(parts[[1]], collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Split each string on Unicode newline sequences.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: omit_empty
arguments.text: True drops empty pieces. False keeps them. NA is truthy and drops them. The value is recycled with str.

translation.details: Newlines are CR, LF, CRLF, NEL, VT, FF, U+2028, and U+2029. A final newline keeps a trailing empty piece unless omit_empty drops it. NA for omit_empty is truthy, so empty pieces are dropped. A missing string is a one-element NA vector.
translation.value: A list of character vectors. A missing string is a one-element NA vector.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_split_lines
parts = stri_split_lines("a\nb")
print('stri_split_lines("a\\nb") returns ' + ", ".join(parts[0]) + ".")
